design_rationale:
TASK 0 — settling a charged-off loan for a laid-off borrower who also has a pending payment-reduction request on her other loan (frozen 2026-10-16 10:20 EDT).

1. WHY IT IS A GOOD TEST. The customer asks one thing: settle her charged-off Grade E loan, spread over as many monthly payments as allowed. Gold needs three writes discovered from policy, not from the customer: (a) the overdue decision on her Reduced Payment Plan request on the other (active Grade C) loan, because the settlement rule says "The settlement amount is not fixed until no Reduced Payment Plan request on the borrower's other Larkspur loan still stands in requested status."; (b) her own record of the installment term on the settlement request, because "The settlement amount is worked out only after the request records, as its plan months, the number of monthly installments the borrower has chosen."; (c) the settlement offer. Each write carries its own multi-factor figure (6 / 4 / 6 factors), reconciled from two loan ledgers (84 loan_transactions rows), document lines and the other loan's standing. Difficulty is reading policy, querying and calculating; there is one tool per problem and no near-synonym tool.

2. SCOPE. Draw (draw_counts --task 0): prerequisite_problems 2, factor_counts [6, 6, 4] -> hardship_ext_rpp_offer_payment 6, hardship_ext_settlement_offer_amount 6, hardship_ext_settlement_installment_term 4. Claimed: Reduced Payment Plan offer terms (state_due), settlement term record (user), settlement offer amount (on_request); tools offer_reduced_payment_plan_00434f76, record_settlement_installments_ebffb995 (owner=user), offer_charged_off_settlement_3f4a16ef. Left for task 1: Servicemember Rate Cap Benefit (end of service record, plan installment lines) and the Temporary Rate Reduction Plan offer; nothing reserved idle.

3. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root hardship_ext_settlement_offer_amount. Edge 1 -> hardship_ext_settlement_installment_term: kind value_input, gate chosen_installments, form state, sentence above (affirmative direction, connective "only after"); condition: the settlement request carries plan_months >= 1 recorded by the borrower; resolved by record_settlement_installments_ebffb995 (owner user). Opening evidence: initial_state.hardship_plans.<P1>.plan_months = '' (empty). Exactly one write of this difficulty records plan months on a settlement request (the servicemember end-of-service record writes plan months only on a Servicemember Rate Cap Benefit). Edge 2 -> hardship_ext_rpp_offer_payment: kind state_gate, gate hardship_plans.status, form state, sentence above (negated direction, connective "not ... until"); condition: no Reduced Payment Plan request of the borrower on another loan in requested status; resolved by offer_reduced_payment_plan_00434f76 (owner agent). Opening evidence: initial_state.hardship_plans.<P2>.status = requested, variant Reduced Payment Plan, loan <L2>. Exactly one write of this difficulty moves a Reduced Payment Plan request out of requested status (the Temporary Rate Reduction Plan offer decides only rate-reduction requests; declining is not a task tool). Derivation: sentence + find_hardship_plans (P2 requested) + the Reduced Payment Plan rule ("the decision is owed whether or not the borrower calls"; the offer records the request as offered) -> the Reduced Payment Plan offer; sentence + P1.plan_months empty + the settlement-term rule ("A borrower settling a charged-off loan records on the pending request, as its plan months, the number of monthly installments chosen") -> the borrower's own record. Topological order: [rpp offer, settlement term] -> settlement offer. The two prerequisites write different plans and neither computation reads the other's plan; swapping them gives the same terminal hash ab08def5647e4e1c and the term recomputes to 3. Deletion sensitivity: without the term record the settlement recomputes to 1159.04 (single-payment price 55, floor 30) instead of 1390.84; without the RPP offer, P2 stays requested (status, decision_date, plan_payment_amount 91.50, start/end dates differ in the terminal state). value_input edges: 1 >= max(2-1,1). user_scenario names neither prerequisite (the other loan appears only in a conditional reaction); every task tool body is one unconditional ctx.update with no status check, so nothing blocks.

4. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Offer writes (subject hardship_plan_offered) inherit hardship_agg_relief_limits, hardship_evt_documents_and_decision, hardship_evt_offer_terms (no gate on this subject: policy_scope) and hardship_settlement.days_since_charge_off (time gate; anchor loans.charged_off_date, relation not_before, duration variants.min_days_since_charge_off, calendar days from the day after the charge-off date, boundary inclusive). Settlement: charged off 2025-12-10, minimum 30 days -> 2026-01-08 (29 days) fails, 2026-01-09 (30) passes, 2026-10-16 = 310 days. RPP: min_days_since_charge_off 0, no charge-off date -> holds on any date. The term record (subject hardship_plan_end_date_set) inherits hardship_scra_benefit, whose gates apply only to hardship_benefit_applied: policy_scope. Request-time gates (one open plan per loan, program usage, status, seasoning) were satisfied when each request was taken: P1 on a charged_off loan with 307 days since charge-off and balance 3863.45 >= 300; P2 on an active loan funded 2024-06-10 (>= 3 months), 27 installments paid (>= 3), 0 days past due on 2026-10-08 (<= 89), principal 1705.93 (>= 500), job_loss qualifying, termination notice on file 2026-10-09 (inside 14 days). RPP decision window: 3 business days after the document -> 2026-10-13, 10-14, 10-15 (10-12 Columbus Day is a Federal Reserve holiday) -> overdue on 2026-10-16 (state_due).

5. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Settlement object: hardship plan P1 on loan L1; charged-off balance = loans.principal_balance 3848.45 + loans.fees_balance 15.00. Fees, priced under the published loan fee figuring (OH schedule_a): returned-payment fee 2025-08-14 11.48 (15.00 x AutoPay share 0.90 x first-return share 0.85), one late fee 2025-08-28 for the 2025-08-12 installment 12.44 (15.00 minimum x AutoPay-history 0.95 x first-late 0.90 x tenure 0.97), returned-payment fee 2025-09-15 13.50 (15.00 x 0.90; an earlier return in the year, so no first-return share), returned-payment fee 2026-08-25 15.00 (no share applies); no further late fee, because a late fee is assessed only on the oldest unpaid installment, at most one per installment, and the 2025-08-12 installment stayed the oldest unpaid one until charge-off. The 2025-09-12 AutoPay debit paid interest, the two fees then due and principal before its 2025-09-15 return reversed all three. Payments 2026-04-20 and 2026-07-17 (30.00 each) paid the three 2025 fees oldest first (loan_fee_paid lines, related_txn_id = fee, source_txn_id = payment) and 22.58 of principal; the 2026-08-21 payment went to principal and was returned 2026-08-25 -> unpaid fees 15.00. Excluded from the balance: the 2025 returned AutoPay debits (reversed), interest (stops at charge-off). RPP object: plan P2 on loan L2; the 2026-10-10 AutoPay debit (207.96) posted and was returned R01 on 2026-10-13 -> amount_past_due 207.96, fee 11.48 (15.00 x AutoPay share 0.90 x first-return share 0.85; not part of the installment base). Tool writes carry the plan id and the loan id.

6. FACTOR CARD (tier taken / evidence / baseline figure from the sensitivity run).
RPP offer (result 91.50; all-baseline 103.98): arrears_base (method) past-due tier, base 207.96 + 207.96/3 = 277.28 vs scheduled installment -> 68.63 [near-miss: the 2026-10-10 posted debit looks paid until its return row is read]; documented_hardship (parameter, multi-source) job_loss AND termination notice -> 40 vs 50 -> 103.98 (held to the 50% ceiling); loan_tenure 27 months -> 2 -> 97.05; rate_grade Grade C -> 1 -> 94.28; prehardship_record 12 scheduled-installment payments in twelve months less 1 returned = 11 -> 3 -> 99.82; autopay_record (multi-source) AutoPay on AND one returned AutoPay debit in six months -> 1 -> 94.28. 40-2-1-3-1 = 33%; 277.28 x 0.33 = 91.50.
Settlement term (result 3; all-baseline 6): balance_term (method) 3863.45 < 6000 -> floor(3863.45/750) = 5 vs 6 -> 4; bounced_payment_cut (multi-source) return 2026-08-25 AND no later payment -> 2 -> 5 [near-miss: the 2026-08-21 payment is a posted payment but precedes the return]; active_loan_arrears L2 past due 6 days -> 1 -> 4; hardship_kind_extension (multi-source) job_loss AND termination notice 2026-10-13 -> +1 -> 2. MN(6, MX(2, 5-2-1+1)) = 3.
Settlement amount (result 1390.84; all-baseline 2704.41): term_pricing (method) linear 55 + 3x2 = 61 vs two-step 70 -> 1738.55; charge_off_age 310 days -> 10 -> 1777.19; good_faith_payments (multi-source) 3 payments, 1 returned -> 3 -> 1506.75 [near-miss: counting all three as standing would give the clean tier 6]; relationship_standing L2 past due 6 days -> 2 -> 1468.11 [near-miss: L2 shows AutoPay on and a posted 10-10 debit]; documented_severity job_loss AND notice -> 5 -> 1584.01; predefault_history 29 posted - 2 returned = 27 -> 5 -> 1584.01. 61-10-3-2-5-5 = 36% (floor 30 not binding); 3863.45 x 0.36 = 1390.84.
Cross-difficulty factors read the loan category (another difficulty's product): rate_grade, prehardship_record, autopay_record, loan_tenure, arrears_base, balance_term, active_loan_arrears, term_pricing, charge_off_age, good_faith_payments, relationship_standing, predefault_history. Multi-source: documented_hardship, autopay_record, bounced_payment_cut, hardship_kind_extension, good_faith_payments, documented_severity. No outcome stamp exists; plan fields read are the reported reason and the recorded term.

7. WORLD ROWS. customers (1), bank_accounts (1: Huntington checking 2593, verified — the AutoPay account; the R01 return does not close it), loans (2), loan_transactions (84: L1 disbursement 2, 27 AutoPay installments, 2 returned debits + returns, 7 fees, 3 post-charge-off payments, 6 fee payments, 1 return, 2 fee-payment reversals; L2 disbursement 2, 27 installments, the 10-10 debit, its return and fee), hardship_plans (2), hardship_plan_events (2 termination notices). Removing the 10-13 return flips arrears_base, autopay_record, relationship_standing and active_loan_arrears; removing the 08-25 return flips the bounced and good-faith tiers; removing either notice drops the documented tiers. Automatic clauses checked: no late fee on the charged-off loan after charge-off (late fees only on active loans); L2's 10-10 installment is inside its 15-day grace (late fee not yet due until 2026-10-26); AutoPay cancellation needs 2 consecutive returns (only one on L2); no acceptance/expiry is due (no offer exists yet).

8. PERSONA. Monica R. Hollister, plain-spoken, laid off in September. Volunteers: settle the old loan, as many monthly payments as allowed, nothing paid today. Given on request: mobile 6145552471 (locator), date of birth 1983-05-27 and ZIP 43207 (3 credentials), email/SSN only if more are needed, reason (laid off; layoff letter uploaded with the Tuesday request), lump vs monthly (monthly, as many as allowed). Passive: confirms her own online request for lower payments on the newer loan only if the representative raises it and lets them proceed; records exactly the installment number the representative gives; repeats the settlement figures, says she will read the offer before accepting, ends the call. No number of gold appears in the persona; she never volunteers a prerequisite.

9. STANDARD SOLUTION AND VERIFICATION. Reads: find_customers(phone) -> verify_customer_identity(phone, dob, zip) -> find_loans -> find_bank_accounts -> find_loan_transactions -> find_loan_servicing_events -> find_hardship_plans -> find_hardship_plan_events. Writes: RPP offer (P2, L2, 207.96, 14.49, 1705.93, 9, 2026-11-10, 2027-01-10, 91.50) -> borrower records plan_months 3 on P1 -> settlement offer (P1, L1, 3863.45, 463.61, 1390.84). Verification: /tmp authoring harness replays gold with the real tools and evaluates each compute on the handling-time world: "B 91.50 U 3 R 1390.84 inst 463.61"; factor baselines as in section 6; "R without U: 1159.04", "R without B: 1390.84"; order swap hashes equal. Probes on scratch copies: see the round 2 probe table (worklog and section 16).

10. RULE <-> COMPUTE SWEEP. Forward: every binding of the three policies quotes a sentence that is verbatim in its rule (scratch sweep: 0 misses). Reverse: each policy's rule sentences are claimed — RPP: scope/overwrite sentence (policy header), decision-owed sentence (trigger, no binding), baseline 2 sentences (pre_plan_installment, result), payment base (loan_past_due, extra_principal_12m, loan_principal, loan_rate_monthly, due_dates_left, payment_base), documented percentage (termination_notices, income_statements, hardship_percent), tenure (tenure_months with the month-completion convention, tenure_points), grade, payment-record, AutoPay ladders, assembly sentence (plan_percent: points subtracted before the percentage is applied once; rounding once on the final figure with the 25.00 floor in result). Settlement term: baseline sentence (result's fall-through 6), starting term (charged-off balance definition, months since charge-off with the charge-off-day convention), returned-payment cut incl. the same-day tie, other-loan cut, extension, assembly ("every reduction that applies is then subtracted from it and every addition that applies added to it, in that order ... held between 2 and 6"). Settlement amount: two prerequisite sentences (chosen_installments; status gate carries no binding), choice sentence (chosen_installments), balance (co_principal/co_fees/charged_off_balance), standard percentage (standard_percent), amount and installment sentence (result; the installment is the tool's plan_payment_amount = amount / recorded installments), term pricing, age (DAYS, day-after counting), good faith, relationship, documented hardship, payment history, assembly (settlement_percent with the 30 floor applied after all subtractions). Rounding: RND only on the final amount in both money policies, matching "rounded to the cent once, on the final figure".

11. XF RECIPE (14 points).
(1) Independence — factor bindings read only evidence and plain bindings: RPP arrears_base reads pre_plan_installment (plain) + its own loan reads; documented_hardship reads its document counts; tenure/grade/payment-record/AutoPay read only their own loan reads; settlement term balance_term reads its own CFIELDs; bounced/arrears/extension read their own evidence; settlement amount term_pricing reads chosen_installments and standard_percent (plain) + pricing_balance (own); no factor reads another factor's binding; results assemble only in plan_percent/result, result, settlement_percent/result.
(2) Assembly stated once, generically, with order: "Where another rule of this policy replaces ..., the replacement takes its place; every point that applies is then subtracted ...", "Where another rule of this policy replaces the program's settlement_max_installments, the replacement takes its place; every reduction ... then subtracted ... every addition ... added", "the replacement is taken first; every point ... is then subtracted ..., never below settlement_floor_pct".
(3) Factor-only quantities defined in their own sentence: payment base, documented percentage, charged-off balance for the term (moved out of the term baseline), term price; baselines name no factor quantity.
(4) Overwrites: RPP retires the RPP installment sentence of hardship_evt_offer_terms with a self-scoped replacement; the settlement term retires only the fragment "for 2 to settlement_max_installments monthly installments" and the settlement amount only the pricing fragment "Charged-Off Settlement Plan sets the settlement amount at settlement_lump_sum_percent of the charged-off balance for one payment, or settlement_installment_percent" — disjoint fragments, each replaced_by naming its own scope; the settlement amount also retires hardship_settlement's flat-percent choice sentence. Each retires a clause that conflicts on this world (base would give 6 installments / 2704.41 / 103.98). No rule defers to a retired clause.
(5) compute_basis verbatim: scratch sweep 0 misses after every edit.
(6) Rounding sentence matches RND placement (final figure only).
(7) Docstrings: effects match bodies (single ctx.update each); no example values (the rate arguments state the format and precision only); no ordering words, no other tool names.
(8) Edge probes: listed in section 9 (absent other loan, current other loan, 30+ days, same-day tie, later payment, single payment, small balance, re-amortization incl. zero rate, AutoPay off); None guards on the other-loan reads, zero-rate guard, MONTHS month-end convention stated in tenure and sale-review sentences, DAYS counting stated, entries counted as payments (not periods), returned payments excluded by explicit return counts.
(9) Method tiers change shape: arrears_base {installment + arrears/3 | annuity on principal | installment}; balance_term {floor(balance/750) | sale_review_months less whole months elapsed | constant 6}; term_pricing {55 + 3(n-1) | constant 55 | step 55/70}. Distinguishing inputs: amount_past_due>0 vs extra principal>=500 vs neither; balance<6000 vs >=6000 & >=18 months vs other; balance>=2000 & 2<=n<6 vs balance<1000 & n>=2 vs other. No two tiers coincide on their reachable domains: round 2 closed the point coincidences (linear at n=6 equal to the two-step 70; flat at n=1 equal to the two-step 55) by ending the linear tier below the program maximum and starting the flat tier at two installments, so linear gives 58..67, flat 55 for n>=2, two-step 70 for n>=2 and 55 for one payment.
(10) Factor ids vs tool names: none of arrears_base, documented_hardship, loan_tenure, rate_grade, prehardship_record, autopay_record, balance_term, bounced_payment_cut, active_loan_arrears, hardship_kind_extension, term_pricing, charge_off_age, good_faith_payments, relationship_standing, documented_severity, predefault_history is a substring of a tool name.
(11) No cross-record date pairing is computed (the other loan's past-due test uses that loan's own fields).
(12) Realism: settlement pricing by term, age, good-faith payments, hardship evidence, relationship and pre-default history is ordinary recovery practice; payment-reduction terms by documented hardship, arrears, tenure, grade, other-account distress and AutoPay are company schedules; seeded loan rows are states the loan charter produces (charge-off at 120 DPD, OH schedule_a fees, AutoPay cancelled after two consecutive returns, fees paid oldest-first, reversals on return); no fee on unbilled interest, no fee after charge-off other than the base's returned-payment fee.
(13) frozen_time '2026-10-16 10:20:00 EDT'; task_tools.py imports only erlbench; every write tool calls ctx.update in its own body; no date maths in tools.
(14) Proof sweep: this dossier, the closure, necessity texts and tracing were regenerated from the verification output after the RPP plan months were corrected to 3 (end date 2027-01-10, base 277.28, 91.50) and after the bank-account read moved the call steps to 8/10/12.

12. REACHABILITY AND CLOSURE. Turn by turn: phone -> profile; three credentials -> verified; loans, bank account, ledgers, plans, documents read; the agent explains the pending RPP request must be decided first, the borrower agrees; the RPP offer is written (state_due); the agent states the longest term (3) and hands over the record tool, the borrower records 3 (her own write, return enters the transcript); the settlement offer is written and its figures told. Everything happens at one frozen time; nothing waits for a payment, document or review. Policy -> tool -> computation -> GT -> terminal: hardship_ext_rpp_offer_payment -> offer_reduced_payment_plan_00434f76 -> step 9 plan_payment_amount 91.50 -> P2 offered; hardship_ext_settlement_installment_term -> record_settlement_installments_ebffb995 -> step 11 plan_months 3 -> P1.plan_months 3; hardship_ext_settlement_offer_amount -> offer_charged_off_settlement_3f4a16ef -> step 13 settlement_amount 1390.84 -> P1 offered. required_documents = charter_scope order.

13. SOLVABILITY VS GT. Step 8: state_due intent from P2 (status requested, request 2026-10-08, document 2026-10-09); discriminator variant 'Reduced Payment Plan'; base preconditions = relief limits / documents & decision / offer terms (policy_scope) + days_since_charge_off bound to loan_id L2. Step 10: on_request intent 'you want to spread the settlement out over as many monthly payments as Larkspur will allow'; hardship_scra_benefit policy_scope. Step 12: intent 'you want to settle it for less than the full balance'; days_since_charge_off bound to loan_id L1 with the 2026-01-08/2026-01-09 boundary.

14. DRAFT FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. Masking compute/expected: the published settlement rule shows two waits — the recorded installment count (absent on P1) and no RPP request in requested status on the other loan (P2 requested) — so the RPP decision and the borrower's record precede the offer; the RPP rule's ladders on the loan/ledger rows give 33% of 277.28 = 91.50; the term rule gives 5 - 2 - 1 + 1 = 3; the amount rule gives 36% of 3863.45 = 1390.84 with installments of 463.61. The draft agrees with gold.

15. EASILY GOT WRONG. Treating the 10-10 AutoPay debit as paid (misses the 10-13 return): arrears base 207.96 -> 68.63 and relationship tier 5 points. Counting the returned 08-21 payment as standing: clean good-faith tier and no bounced cut. Pricing the settlement off the flat 70%: 2704.41. Offering the settlement first: priced as a single payment (P1 has no term) and the RPP request still pending. Recording a term of 6 (program maximum) or 5 (ignoring cuts).

16. ROUND 2 PROBE TABLE (scratch copies of each step world; the worklog carries the same table). B (reduced payment, gold 91.50): loan rows swapped 91.50 (CFIELD by loan_id); termination notice moved to the settlement plan only 103.98 and no document on the request 103.98 (absent: program percentage); no arrears with 600.00 additional principal posted in the window 66.39 (re-amortized base); the same payment returned 68.63 (netted: scheduled-installment base, as the rule now says "less any of them returned"); no arrears, no prepayment 68.63; zero rate with prepayment 62.55 (principal divided by due dates, no division by zero); the AutoPay return moved to exactly six months before the decision 88.73 (outside: the rule now states that a row dated exactly that many months before falls outside); funded on the 31st, 23 whole months 94.28 (day-of-month rule). U (settlement term, gold 3): loan rows swapped 3; other loan paid_off 4 and no other loan 4 (status filter, absent tier); payment posted the same day as the latest return 3 (stated tie rule: not after it); posted the day after 4; no return in six months 5; ledger reversed 3; no charge-off date 3 (stated: counts no months since charge-off; not reachable for a charged-off loan). R (settlement amount, gold 1390.84): loan rows swapped 1390.84; plan months empty 1159.04 (one payment); other loan paid_off 1468.11; other loan current 1274.94; the return dated exactly six months before 1274.94 (outside, as stated); an extra returned scheduled installment 1390.84 (history still >= 24 net); rows reversed 1390.84; no charge-off date 1777.19 (stated: counts no days). The other active loan read by U and R is single because Larkspur lets a borrower hold at most two open personal loans at a time and takes no new loan application while any of the borrower's loans is charged off (the loan product's own base rules), stated in those business words in both rules, so no second active row exists to reorder. Term-pricing probes (round 2): 6 installments 1738.55 (two-step 70, not linear); 5 installments 1622.65 (linear 67); balance 900 with 3 installments and with one payment both 270.00 (flat 55 and two-step 55 both held up by the settlement floor).

17. ROUND 3. P1's payment-record rule now names scheduled-installment payments, as computed (probe: a partial-installment payment in the window leaves 91.50). P2's charge-off-date guard now sits in its starting-term sentence and its six-month look-back boundary in its returned-payment cut sentence; P3's guard sits in its charge-off age sentence; the single-other-active-loan statement sits inside each other-loan sentence. Zero amounts are stated: the reduced payment is never below its minimum, the settlement term never below its minimum installments, and the settlement amount never 0.00 because the program's minimum balance and the floor percentage hold it above zero. Round 3 probes (worklog): as in section 16, plus the partial-installment decoy 91.50, the six-month boundary for U 5, 6 installments 1738.55 and 5 installments 1622.65. Gold unchanged.

18. ROUND 4. Every hold of the charter was checked for a reachable world in which no write of this difficulty can lift it. The settlement's wait on the other loan's Reduced Payment Plan request is lifted by the reduced-payment offer whenever that request can be offered; where it cannot, the rule now states the outcome: the settlement request is handed to the hardship desk instead of being priced in that contact. In this world the request is eligible and offered (step 9), so the tree and every scored value are unchanged.

19. ROUND 5 (renderer source scan). The settlement-term countdown tier now reads exactly as computed (sale_review_months less the whole calendar months elapsed since the charge-off, months completed on the charge-off day of the month); the reduced payment's shared look-back sentence is gone, each of its windowed factor sentences (payment base, payment record, AutoPay) now carrying its own boundary, and the payment base states how due dates left are counted; the outcome sentence after the settlement's wait on the other loan's request no longer names the action that clears it. Gold and every sensitivity unchanged.

20. ROUND 6 (KB audit source items). The reduced payment's ceiling is stated as taken on the loan's own scheduled installment on the decision date, never on a payment base put in its place, which is what the compute does (pre_plan_installment); the settlement term's bounds are stated as the program's own minimum and maximum, never a starting term put in their place; the single-other-loan reason is stated as a company fact in business words. Gold and every sensitivity unchanged.

21. ROUND 7 (seed re-priced from the published loan rules). Both installments are now the level payment on the amount financed at the base rate (Grade E 224.85, Grade C 207.96), unchanged by AutoPay; interest accrues at the AutoPay-discounted rate while AutoPay is on, actual/365, and every interest and principal portion, both principal histories (charged-off principal 3848.45 after 22.58 of post-charge-off principal; Grade C 1705.93), the amounts past due (899.40, 207.96) and both APRs were re-derived. Fee rows carry the published fee shares (11.48, 12.44, 13.50, 15.00 on the charged-off loan; 11.48 on the Grade C loan); the three later late fees are removed because a late fee is charged only on the oldest unpaid installment, once, and that installment stayed 2025-08-12 until charge-off. AutoPay enrollment records sit on both loans' funding dates and the charged-off loan's system cancellation (consecutive returns) on 2025-09-15, read by the new find_loan_servicing_events step. Gold moved with the seed: 91.50, 3, 1390.84 / 463.61 on 3863.45; both prerequisites are still unmet at the opening and every factor still bears weight.
user_scenario:
You are Monica R. Hollister, 43, a warehouse scheduler from Columbus, Ohio, who was laid off in September 2026. You talk plainly and a bit wearily, you apologize when you don't know the lending terms, and you like to have numbers repeated back to you once. You are calling Larkspur Lending about your old personal loan, the one that went to collections last winter after you fell behind: you want to settle it for less than the full balance, and because money is tight you want to spread the settlement out over as many monthly payments as Larkspur will allow. You are not paying anything today and you are not asking for anything to be waived or forgiven beyond the settlement itself.

To find your profile, give your mobile number, 6145552471. When the representative asks you to confirm your identity, give your date of birth as 1983-05-27 and your ZIP code as 43207; only if they say that is not enough do you add your email, monica.hollister@outlook.com, or the last four of your Social Security number, 2836. You do not know your account numbers or balances by heart and you ask the representative to look them up. If you are asked why you need help, you say you were laid off in September and that you uploaded your layoff letter with the settlement request you sent online on Tuesday. If you are asked whether you want one lump-sum payment or monthly payments, you say monthly payments, as many as they will let you have.

If the representative brings up your other, newer Larkspur loan, you confirm that yes, you asked online last week for lower payments on that one too after the layoff, and you tell them to go ahead with whatever has to be done on it; when they tell you the payment that comes out of it, you say that sounds like something you can manage. If the representative explains that you have to record your choice of installments yourself and hands that step over to you, you do it on the spot: you want the longest term available, so you record exactly the number of monthly installments the representative tells you is the most you can choose, never a number of your own.

When the representative tells you the settlement amount and what each monthly settlement payment would be, you repeat the figures back once, say you will read the offer over before accepting it, thank them, and end the call.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.plan_payment_amount: Value 91.50. Factors: payment base (arrears method) = 207.96 + 207.96 / 3 = 277.28 because amount_past_due is 207.96 after the 2026-10-13 R01 return of the 2026-10-10 AutoPay debit; documented-hardship percentage 40 (job_loss request with termination notice recorded 2026-10-09); tenure points 2 (27 whole months 2024-06-10 -> 2026-10-08); grade points 1 (Grade C); payment-record points 3 (12 scheduled-installment payments posted in the twelve months before the decision less the one returned = 11); AutoPay points 1 (AutoPay enrolled, one returned AutoPay debit in six months). argument_uniqueness_tracing.settlement_amount: Value 1390.84. Factors: term price 61 (balance 3863.45 >= 2000.00 and 3 installments: 55 + 3 x 2); charge-off age points 10 (310 days from 2025-12-10 to 2026-10-16); good-faith points 3 (payments 2026-04-20, 2026-07-17, 2026-08-21 in six months, the last returned 2026-08-25); relationship points 2 (other active loan past due 207.96, next due 2026-10-10, 6 days back); documented-hardship points 5 (job_loss with termination notice); payment-history points 5 (29 scheduled installments posted less 2 returned = 27 >= 24). Percentage 61 - 10 - 3 - 2 - 5 - 5 = 36 (above the 30 floor); 3863.45 x 36 / 100 = 1390.84.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The settlement request carries no recorded number of installments at the opening: its plan_months field is empty, so chosen_installments falls back to a single payment.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The borrower's own write (step 11) sets plan_months = 3 on the request; chosen_installments becomes 3 and the term price moves from 55 (single payment) to 61.

edges.condition: No hardship plan of the borrower on another loan with variant Reduced Payment Plan is in requested status.
edges.policy_source: The settlement amount is not fixed until no Reduced Payment Plan request on the borrower's other Larkspur loan still stands in requested status.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The borrower's other loan carries a Reduced Payment Plan request still in requested status at the opening (requested 2026-10-08, decision overdue since 2026-10-15).
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The Reduced Payment Plan offer (step 9) moves that request to offered, so no Reduced Payment Plan request of the borrower stands in requested status.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two prerequisites touch different plans (the offer writes the Reduced Payment Plan request on the Grade C loan; the borrower's write sets plan_months on the settlement request) and neither computation reads the other's plan. Replaying the gold with the two prerequisite pairs swapped (U then B) gives the same terminal hash ab08def5647e4e1c as B then U, and the settlement term recomputes to 3 under both orders; the root comes last in either order.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the borrower's installment record leaves plan_months empty: chosen_installments = 1, the term price falls back to the single-payment 55 and the settlement amount recomputes to 1159.04 instead of 1390.84; the request's plan_months stays empty in the terminal state.

Skipping the Reduced Payment Plan offer leaves that request in requested status in the terminal state (status, decision_date, plan_payment_amount 91.50, start/end dates all differ) and the settlement's waited-on state never holds; the settlement figure itself does not read that plan (state_gate).

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario raises only the settlement: the newer loan and its payment request appear only inside a conditional reaction ('If the representative brings up your other, newer Larkspur loan, you confirm ...'), and the installment step only inside 'If the representative explains that you have to record your choice of installments yourself and hands that step over to you'. No policy id, tool name, status, decision deadline or ordering is mentioned.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: task_tools.py: offer_charged_off_settlement_3f4a16ef is a single ctx.update on the plan row with no read of other plans, no status check and no refusal path; it writes the offer even while plan_months is empty or the other loan's request is still requested. record_settlement_installments_ebffb995 and offer_reduced_payment_plan_00434f76 are likewise single unconditional updates.
